plant.name: Plant
plant.intro: Pipe specs, isometrics, process equipment with nozzles and a layout check. A drafting aid, not an engineering approval: the person responsible for the plant owns the specs, the limits and the drawings.
equip.intro: Generic equipment of the right proportions, with nozzles (no maker's dimensions). Add what the plant has; the table is kept in this browser and goes out as an IFC file with a port at every nozzle.
specs.intro: A spec is found by a run's material and class. These come with the add-on; the sizes and walls are from the public tables.
iso.intro: Select pipe runs in the model, then save their isometric: 30° projection, every leg dimensioned, elevations, valves, welds and a bill of materials. Not to scale.
layout.intro: Checks the equipment table above, and equipment placed in the model from the library, for overlaps, aisles, the space needed beside each item and floor load. The limits are yours.
export.iso.svg: Isometric of the selected pipe runs (SVG)
export.iso.dxf: Isometric of the selected pipe runs (DXF)
cmd.spec-check: Check the selected runs against their pipe spec
cmd.route: Route a pipe between two nozzles
done.iso: Use Export to save the isometric.
err.noruns: Select one or more pipe runs first.
err.noequipment: There is no equipment in the table yet.
need.write: Placing equipment in the open model and routing a run between nozzles need BimCraft add-on API 1.1, which this build does not have yet. Save the equipment as an IFC file and open it for now.
note.write.yes: This BimCraft can write into the model: placing and routing are available.
props.size.bad: this run's size {size} is not allowed
finding.spec-size: Size {size} is not allowed by {spec} ({min} to {max}).
finding.spec-valve: A {kind} valve is not allowed by {spec} at size {size}.
finding.spec-bend: A turn is tighter than {spec} allows.
layout.aisle: {a} and {b} are {gap} mm apart; the least aisle is {min} mm.
layout.blocked-access: {name}: the {side} side needs {clear} mm clear, but {by} is in it.
layout.floor-load: {name} loads the floor with {load} kg/m²; the limit is {limit}.
done.place: {n} placed in the model: one undo step.
done.place.none: Nothing to place: every item in the table is in the model already.
route.intro: Choose two ports of the model and a spec: the router finds a clear route between them that leaves each nozzle straight out, avoids the equipment in the table that is in the model, and bends as little as it can.
route.few: The model has fewer than two ports to route between. Place equipment with nozzles first.
route.found: A route of {len} mm with {bends} bends and {climbs} vertical legs.
route.err.size: That size is not in the spec's tables.
route.err.blocked-start: The first nozzle faces into something: there is no room to leave it.
route.err.blocked-end: The second nozzle faces into something: there is no room to arrive at it.
route.err.no-route: No clear route was found between these ports.
route.err.too-big: The area is too large to search; move the two ports closer.
route.err.axis: A nozzle must face along X, Y or Z.
route.nowrite: Putting the run into the model needs a run writer in BimCraft's add-on API that this build does not have yet. The points are the route's corners in the storey's own millimetres (the last number is the height above the level).
route.hint: Open the Plant tab, choose two ports and press Find a route.
iso.bom.title: BILL OF MATERIALS
iso.note.dims.ftin: Dimensions are lengths along the pipe center line, in feet and inches
iso.note.dims.mm: Dimensions are lengths along the pipe center line, in millimeters
err.place.noequip: There is no equipment to place.
err.place.nostorey: The model has no level to place it on.
spec.starter.cs40.name: Carbon steel, Sch 40, general service
spec.starter.cs40.notes: Welded and threaded pipe; stub-in branches up to a quarter of the header.
spec.starter.cs80.name: Carbon steel, Sch 80, heavy wall
spec.starter.cs80.notes: For higher pressure or a corrosion allowance.
spec.starter.cu-l.name: Copper tube, type L
spec.starter.pvc40.name: PVC, Sch 40
spec.starter.pex9.name: PEX tubing, SDR 9
cmd.route.draw: Draw the route last found as a pipe run
route.drawn: Drew a {spec} run, size {size}, {len} mm long, as one change. Undo takes it back.
route.err.storey: Both ports must be on the same level to draw the run.
route.draw.note: BimCraft has no process system of its own: the run goes into the pipe system you choose, in the spec's material and class. Its ends join the nozzles they touch.
proc.intro: Load a process model (process.json) made in CadCraft, Super or by the assistant; then check the pipe runs against it: line sizes, lengths, bends and valves give each line's velocity and pressure drop, and anything the P&ID has to change is listed.
proc.err.none: There is no process model loaded. Load a process.json in the Process model section.
proc.err.file: That file is not a CadCraft process model.
done.proc: {lines} lines worked out, {linked} newly linked. {errors} errors, {warnings} warnings. {first}
proc.edit: {ln}: pipe is {size}, velocity {v} m/s, drop {dp} bar
btn.layout.process: Add the model's equipment to the table
proc.nolayout: This process model has no 3D layout.
proc.layout.added: {n} pieces of equipment added to the table; place them with Place equipment.
wire.in: A process model arrived: line {what} is {size}. {n} pipe runs differ from the P&ID sizes.
wire.out: Line {ln} is now {size} in 3D. The process model was updated and sent to the P&ID.
wire.applied: {n} pipe runs changed to the P&ID sizes (one undo step).
btn.apply.sizes: Apply the P&ID sizes to the pipe runs
cmd.process-apply-sizes: Apply the P&ID sizes to the pipe runs
wire.in.model: A process model arrived ({what}). {n} pipe runs differ from the P&ID sizes.
sec.p4: Plant with pipes, batch schedule, live values
p4.place.intro: Put the process model's layout in the model: the equipment, then each pipe routed between the equipment's nozzles. One undo step each.
p4.place.btn: Place the plant and its pipes
p4.place.done: Placed {equipment} equipment, drew {runs} pipe runs, left {skipped} out.
p4.why.nowrite: This BimCraft cannot draw pipes yet.
p4.why.notplaced: one end is not in the model
p4.why.noport: no free nozzle on one end
p4.why.storey: the two ends are on different storeys
p4.why.route: no route found round the equipment
p4.batch.intro: Show a batch recipe in the 4D panel: each step is a task on its equipment, found in the model by its tag.
p4.batch.no4d: Open the 4D tab first: the schedule goes there.
p4.batch.done: {tasks} tasks, {hours} hours, sent to the 4D panel.
p4.live.intro: Readings as CSV with a header row tag,time,value,quality. The equipment with that tag is tinted in the 3D view by its state.
p4.live.note: Read only. Nothing here controls equipment and nothing here is an alarm system.
live3d.notags: The equipment table has no tags to match.
live.lede: Show readings from a plant or a building on the drawing. Read only: nothing here writes to a device or raises an alarm. A device on a public address needs your yes for that host.
live.check.done: {tags} tags on {devices} devices checked: {problems} things to look at.
live.bridge.none: Reading a device needs CadCraft Studio: a browser page cannot open a plant network connection. Use a CSV of readings meanwhile.
live.bridge.noproto: This Studio does not read {protocol} yet.
live.note: Read-only plant and building data, for viewing and comparison. Not an alarm system or a safety function.
timer.lede: Keep the HAZOP session on time. Set the minutes for each node, start the clock on the node the team is discussing, and move on when it is done. Over-time is shown, never forced.
timer.none: No node yet. Draw a node boundary with PIDNODE first.
timer.note: A team study aid. It records the time; it does not decide that a node is finished.
opt.lede: Try many settings of the process model and rank them. Name the unit and the parameter to vary, the range, and what to minimise. Computers you connected in Studio (Settings, Rendering, other computers) solve variants too; the rest are solved here.
opt.nonodes: No other computer is connected: every variant is solved here.
opt.nomodel: No process model yet. Bring one in from the process file first.
opt.badjson: The study is not valid JSON: {why}
opt.done: {n} variants: {remote} solved on other computers, {local} here, {failed} could not be solved.
calc.option.pick: Choose a fitting from the draft table…
